title: growth_district_live_count's Terminal-only filter still unpinned (r1 W3 unaddressed) — a routers-count-too mutation passes all 261 core tests
detail: The district cap's measured side counts live TERMINALS only; routers must never consume budget. Mutation-verified: dropping the Terminal filter passes the entire suite, so the r1 W3 warning remains open at head.
recommended_fix: Add a draw/step-level pin: place routers inside a district near its cap, assert the district stays eligible (e.g. extend test_growth_district_seed_draw_cap_and_exhaustion with in-district routers).

title: One former partition copy-paste site left unconverted: growth_test's `one` fixture hand-builds district_tiles instead of calling map_board_partition
detail: r1 counted 5 hand-rolled partition sites; the fold converted 4. This one falsifies both the map.odin comment ('every test fixture call map_board_partition') and the PR claim 'loader + all fixtures — one definition'.
recommended_fix: Replace the two hand-built lines with `map_board_partition(&one, context.temp_allocator)` (identical output for a 1-district/1-tile board, but drift-proof).

title: Loader's partition invocation unasserted — deleting map_board_partition from map_board_load passes all 261 core tests (r1 W4 residual)
evidence:
core/map.odin:417: 	map_board_partition(&b, allocator)
The loader tests assert districts/candidates but never district_tiles, e.g. core/map_test.odin:138-147 (test_map_board_load_districts_parse):
	testing.expectf(t, len(b.districts) == 3, "3 districts expected, got %d", len(b.districts))
	testing.expectf(t, b.districts[0].name == "Dublin" && b.districts[0].kind == .City, "district 0 parse wrong: %v %v", ...)
(no district_tiles assertion in any map_board_load test). Mutation check (04ef6a9 exported to /tmp, the call replaced by a comment): `odin test core -o:speed` → "Finished 261 tests in 1.335024s. All tests were successful."
detail: The shared builder is itself pinned via fixtures, but the loader's wiring is not: a regression that skips/reorders the partition call yields an empty district_tiles board with a fully green unit suite (only the golden harness would trap).
recommended_fix: In a map_board_load test, assert len(b.district_tiles) == len(b.districts) and that the partition covers len(b.candidates) memberships.

title: Loader tests free district names cross-allocator: map_board_load(temp_allocator) + map_board_destroy delete(d.name) → tracking allocator reports bad frees
evidence:
core/map_test.odin:134: 	b, err := map_board_load(transmute([]u8)src, &bal, context.temp_allocator)
core/map.odin:356: 	append(&b.districts, Map_District{name = strings_clone(name, allocator), kind = kind, pos = {f32(px), f32(py)}})
core/map.odin:167-169:
	for d in b.districts {
		delete(d.name)
	}
`odin test core` at 04ef6a9 emits (identically at 93333cd):
	[WARN ] ... :: core.test_map_board_load_districts_parse
	        +++ bad free        @ 0x... [map.odin:168:map_board_destroy()]
detail: strings carry no allocator, so delete(d.name) frees via context.allocator while the tests cloned names via temp_allocator — the tracking allocator flags three bad frees per loader test. Production (harness board_load uses context.allocator) is unaffected; test-only noise from the feature commit.
recommended_fix: Pass context.allocator to map_board_load in the loader tests (boards are tiny), or give map_board_destroy an explicit allocator parameter for the name frees.
